title: Commands, hooks, and automation guide
summary: This intermediate reference explains why the requested source correction cannot yet be applied safely and identifies the evidence required to complete it without changing unaffected material.
prerequisites: The exact current contents of the resource being corrected
The previous and replacement source URLs with a first-party change record
The repository revision against which the correction will be reviewed

sections.title: Answer before editing
paragraphs: For an intermediate practitioner asking what should be corrected now, the answer is UNKNOWN. Do not apply a content correction until the existing resource, the changed external source, and evidence of what changed are available.

The supplied material does not identify which external source moved or exceeded its review cadence. Its previous URL, replacement URL, publisher, previous verification date, and affected guide passages are all UNKNOWN. Consequently, the requested statement naming the changed source and its effect cannot be completed without inventing facts.

The technical environment is also UNKNOWN. No supported tool name, command syntax, hook lifecycle, automation mechanism, configuration key, permission requirement, output, or failure mode can be added.
sections.callout: Next action: obtain the exact baseline resource and the first-party source-change record before editing any existing guide content.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: First, retrieve the exact current JSON file from the revision being corrected. If the file or revision is unavailable, stop and request both from the repository owner. Do not reconstruct the baseline from its filename.

Second, compare the previously cited source with its replacement or first-party revision history. Record the source title, old URL, replacement URL, publisher, previous verification date, and the statements or procedures affected by the change. If either source version or a first-party change record is unavailable, mark the impact UNKNOWN and request that evidence rather than changing technical instructions.

Third, edit only the citation record and the passages demonstrably affected by the source change. If a proposed technical claim lacks direct first-party support, omit that proposed claim and request an authoritative source. Preserve every unaffected field and passage from the baseline.

Finally, serialize the result as one JSON object and parse the complete file as JSON text. If parsing reports a syntax error, inspect the reported location, correct invalid delimiters or string escaping, and parse the complete file again before submission.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A completed correction must provide the original resource revision, the identity and previous URL of the changed citation, its verified replacement URL, a first-party record establishing the change, and a comparison showing which guide passages were affected.

Verify success by reviewing a diff against the supplied baseline. The diff should contain only the corrected source record and content directly affected by that source. If unrelated wording, metadata, or procedures changed, restore them from the baseline and review the diff again.

Verify serialization by parsing the complete file as JSON text. Successful parsing must return one object. If parsing throws a syntax error or returns another value type, correct the serialization and repeat the check. Technical accuracy remains UNKNOWN until the subject-matter sources and resulting procedures are independently checked.
